decisions.rationale: Operator instruction after three consecutive Code-stage idle-timeout failures on the live phase 35.1 DevFlow run (120s idle timeout, aborted_tools terminal_reason each time); a fourth attempt was judged likely to fail identically.

decisions.decision: Still execute Task 2 (actually run the drill) rather than fabricate 35.1-DRILL.md by hand.
decisions.rationale: The drill's fixtures are throwaway git repos scaffolded under $TMPDIR via scripts/unattended-drill.sh, guarded by the same refuse-inside-this-checkout guard as scripts/scratch-dogfood-repo.sh (T-23-01) — verified by demonstration, exit 1, nothing created inside the checkout. They never touch this repository, so running the drill is not the 'no more dogfooding' the operator meant. A hand-written DRILL.md would fabricate the run record that must be traceable to real events/captures — the exact failure plan 35.1-04's key_links exist to prevent.

decisions.decision: Adopted a stranded executor's already-committed Task 1 + Task 3 work over a duplicate hand-written version.
decisions.rationale: A prior subagent had already completed both tasks and even run the drill once, but its commits (329406e, 3fa896d) were stranded in its own dead worktree (branch worktree-agent-aa8b892e8b0eb81a1) and never merged back — the phase branch showed zero new commits, which read as 'no work done' until the sub-worktree was found and inspected. The stranded script's plan-checkpoint detection was also more correct than the independently hand-written duplicate's (it greps one specific generated plan file; the duplicate grepped the whole .planning/ tree and would have false-matched CONTEXT.md's own locked-decision text). Merged via `git merge --no-ff worktree-agent-aa8b892e8b0eb81a1` (commit 5e15457); the hand-written duplicate was discarded.

GSD's checkpoint_handling reads 'chain flag OR user preference — same boolean' (gsd-core/workflows/execute-phase.md). With auto_mode:true, the persistent preference alone satisfied that OR in BOTH arms, so the ephemeral chain flag under test was never the deciding variable and the first executed run (before this fix) measured nothing — its own evidence file self-reported this as a failed measurement.

decisions.decision: Removed `reached_validate` from the compact checkpoint-comparison string the drill uses for its arms-agree negative-control check.
decisions.rationale: It is a downstream consequence of the checkpoint decision, not the checkpoint decision itself. Including it let the two arms register as 'different' for a reason unrelated to auto-approval (auto_approved=yes/surfaced=yes/reached_validate=no vs =yes/=yes/=yes), so the drill's FAILURE-3/3 self-check (both arms observed the same thing => broken measurement) stayed silent on a run where BOTH arms had, in fact, auto-approved. The comparison is now over checkpoint behaviour alone; reached_validate is still reported in the evidence table, just not part of the discrimination test.
